title: Navigation World Models as Group Actions
claim: Models should satisfy group-action axioms (identity, inverse, composition); adding our regularization makes these observable conditions hold where the baseline fails.
layout: 3 columns, top definition and bottom baseline-vs-ours rows, dashed dividers
description: A wide figure with a bold title, "Action-faithful world models should admit a group action," and an italic subtitle. Below it are three rounded panels: (a) Identity, (b) Inverse Consistency, (c) Compatibility. In each panel, the top half shows the principle with fisheye robot-navigation photos linked by arrows. Examples are a=0 giving no drift, a then -a giving recovery, and two action sequences with equal sums reaching the same endpoint. Green pill labels such as "No Drift", "Recover" and "Same Net Motion" mark the expected result. A dashed line separates the bottom half, which has two rows: NWM (baseline) and NWM+GA (Ours). Each row has small photos and a 2-D trajectory plot with orange and green markers. The baseline is labeled in orange with drift, incomplete recovery or mismatch. Ours is labeled in green with reduced drift, improved recovery or compatible outcomes. Blue and red arrows show the two decompositions in (c).
caption: Consequences of group-action-faithful dynamics. Identity, inverse consistency, and compatibility are observable conditions implied by the group-action formulation. Representative examples illustrate that GA regularization reduces zero-action drift, improves forward--inverse recovery, and yields more compatible outcomes under equivalent action decompositions.
abstract: Navigation video world models have achieved strong visual realism, but this does not ensure that their dynamics are truly governed by actions. In this work, we argue that action faithfulness should be understood through the compositional structure of actions, which in many embodied settings follows a group structure (e.g., SE(2) for navigation). Based on this insight, we formalize action-conditioned navigation world modeling as realizing a group action on the state space, providing a principled criterion for evaluating dynamics beyond visual quality. To operationalize this framework, we propose a unified approach that enforces identity, inverse, and composition consistency via latent-space regularization with synthesized supervision, avoiding additional data collection. We further introduce two metrics: Group-Action Consistency (GAC) and Group-Action Robustness (GAR), to evaluate structural correctness and rollout stability. Extensive experimental results show that our method consistently improves both GAC and GAR across representative video world model backbones in the navigation setting without degrading perceptual quality.
